title: FF-INT8: Efficient Forward-Forward DNN Training on Edge Devices with INT8 Precision
problem: Forward-Forward (FF) algorithm replaces backpropagation's backward pass but still requires heavy memory/compute for activation storage and gradient computation; INT8 quantization for training remains unexplored despite success in inference.
motivation: Edge devices have severe memory and energy constraints; FF reduces memory by avoiding backward-pass activation storage, but further optimization via INT8 quantization can unlock practical edge training.
method: The approach combines the Forward-Forward training method (which trains layers one at a time instead of using backpropagation) with INT8 quantization (using 8-bit integers instead of full-precision numbers), reducing memory and computation needs on edge devices. Training layers sequentially keeps gradients—the values that adjust network weights—stable when using low-bit numbers, because each layer processes independently. A look-ahead mechanism at each layer helps recover accuracy that would otherwise be lost from using fewer bits. The method is tested on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, a compact edge device with limited resources.
key_novelty: This is the first method that applies INT8 quantization to training neural networks, using the Forward-Forward algorithm's layer-by-layer approach to keep gradients stable and a look-ahead refinement to recover accuracy.
contributions: 4.6% faster training via FF-INT8 on Jetson Orin Nano
Competitive accuracy vs. state-of-the-art through look-ahead scheme
limitations: Evaluation limited to Jetson Orin Nano; generalization to other edge accelerators and larger models not discussed.
primary_theme: INT8 quantized edge training via Forward-Forward
